assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle for cells (P granules, nucleoli, multivalent-interaction scaling) gives a clear physical principle, phase behaviour and thermodynamics, applied to cellular compartmentalization without membranes. It is quantitative, generalizes widely and has opened large new capabilities in cell biology and disease research, which fits my physicist's criteria.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the foundational 2009 P-granule discovery, and Rosen and Li et al. gave the multivalent-polymer framework. Pappu and Mittag contribute essential physical-chemistry theory and sequence grammar, but a three-person prize can plausibly be built from Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen. I would want the committee to probe who first articulated the phase-separation framing versus the later multivalency work.
assessment.maturity: Strong and independent confirmation across many labs over more than 15 years, with the core concept stable. The field is still debating physiological relevance, condensate versus aggregate, and some in vitro assay artefacts, so recognition is timely but not beyond criticism.
uncertainties: Whether all reported cellular condensates are true equilibrium phase separation, versus other assemblies.
Allocation of credit between the cell-biology discovery and the polymer-physics framework.
I rely on my own recollection of the literature and have not verified the dates or priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity to hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system to degrade targeted proteins is a new pharmacological modality, converting 'undruggable' targets into druggable ones. The chemistry principle (bifunctional ternary-complex formation, cooperative binding) is clear and it has unmistakably opened unforeseen opportunities, with compounds now in late-stage clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept (2001 onward); Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and ternary-complex structural rationale. The thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue discoveries (Handa, Ito, Gray, others) are a distinct but related line, and a clean three-person split between PROTACs and glues is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is progressing (e.g. phase 3 data) but approvals are still pending, so the medical impact is not yet fully proven. The chemical concept is well confirmed by many groups.
uncertainties: Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be one citation or are separate discoveries.
Clinical approval status is uncertain to me; I have not verified current trial outcomes.
Priority and credit for the cereblon mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair to another without double-strand breaks, with chemistry-driven design (evolved deaminases fused to Cas9 nickase). This is a conceptually clear and original chemical-biology invention with large therapeutic potential and a human clinical translation already under way.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual driver and inventor of the approach, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainees. The independent Target-AID work by Nishida and Kondo complicates priority a little but does not undermine a Liu-centred award. Recognition of CRISPR in 2020 means the committee needs to articulate a distinct citation.
assessment.maturity: Clinical-stage applications and broad adoption in research confirm robustness. Long-term safety (off-target deamination) remains under evaluation, though the basic invention is firmly established.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with Liu's prime-editing candidate, which may be better treated together.
Priority relative to Target-AID.
Whether the committee would rather cite Liu alone or add co-inventors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view explains how proteins fold quickly despite an astronomical conformational space, resolving Levinthal's paradox through statistical mechanics. This is the type of underlying physical principle I value, and it unifies theory with experiments on folding kinetics and has shaped protein design and prediction.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) developed the funnel/minimal frustration theory; Dill introduced the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model framework. Fersht provided experimental mapping. Credit is distributed, and three of the five names can represent the central theory.
assessment.maturity: Concept well established for decades and widely accepted, so timing is mature, though the 2024 prize on protein design and structure prediction partly overlaps and may make the committee view it as already covered.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize.
Which theory strand (funnel, hydrophobic collapse, experimental phi-value analysis) is decisive.
Priority between Bryngelson-Wolynes and Onuchic contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Scaffolded DNA origami and programmable DNA nanostructures show rational bottom-up design at the molecular scale, programming shape and function via base pairing. It is original and generative, linking to molecular machines and nanodevices, though the principle follows from Seeman's structural DNA nanotechnology.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami paper is decisive, Winfree contributed algorithmic self-assembly and the theoretical underpinnings, and Yan pioneered DNA nanostructure design. Seeman, a founder, is deceased, and this narrows the possible laureates and complicates fair credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature with thousands of designs and a growing set of applications, but practical, widely impactful uses (e.g. drug delivery, nanofabrication) are still emerging.
uncertainties: Seeman's death and the reflection of his foundational role.
Whether applications justify recognition now.
Credit split with Yin, Shih and others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single molecules electrically through nanopores uses ionic current blockades as a direct physical readout. It started as a conceptual idea (Deamer and Branton) and was realized through protein-pore engineering (Bayley) and led to long-read sequencing technology with broad impact. It is also physics-heavy, matching my interests.
assessment.attribution: Branton, Deamer and Church-era ideas date from the 1990s; Kasianowicz demonstrated polynucleotide translocation in 1996; Bayley engineered pores and Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled motion. The credit is contested among at least five people, and I would need the committee to sort out who made the decisive step.
assessment.maturity: The technology is commercially deployed and independently confirmed, so maturity is high; recognition is now plausible. The field-defining sequencing impact may be viewed as belonging partly to medicine or physiology.
uncertainties: Priority dispute between Kasianowicz, Deamer, Branton and Akeson.
Whether the sequencing application is chemistry rather than technology development.
Roles of company work (Oxford Nanopore) versus academic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials combine near-quantum accuracy with force-field cost, enabling molecular dynamics at scales previously unreachable. It is a quantitative method with a clear principle (symmetry-adapted regression on local environments) and strongly generative potential across chemistry and materials science.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello's 2007 neural-network potential began the modern line, Bartók, Csányi and colleagues introduced Gaussian approximation potentials. Parrinello's name is also tied to Car-Parrinello and metadynamics candidates, which could make the committee prefer a separate framing.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing and widely adopted, though foundational models are evolving and the field's end state is not settled. The 2024 prize involved AI in chemistry, so timing relative to that is a question.
uncertainties: Premature if the methods are still evolving rapidly (universal potentials).
Overlap with the Parrinello candidates B047 and B053.
Accuracy limits for reactions and long-range effects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiencies from a few percent to above 25 percent within a decade. This is an extraordinary change in capability that opens previously unforeseen opportunities in photovoltaics and light-emitting devices, with interesting defect and ion-transport physics.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell in 2009, Park and Gratzel made the solid-state step in 2012, and Snaith's group boosted efficiency in the thin-film architecture; Kanatzidis, Seok and Gratzel are also strong contributors. Credit is crowded, and the choice of three is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Rapid progress is clear, but operational stability, lead toxicity and commercial scale-up remain unresolved, so the impact may be premature for a prize now.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and commercial viability are uncertain.
Whether Gratzel and Kanatzidis should displace any of the three proposed names.
Whether the discovery is mostly materials engineering after the first report.
